why: Maximise the minimum: if cows can be d apart they can also be d - 1 apart, so 'can k cows be placed with every gap >= d?' is true then false, and the answer is the last true d. The check is greedy: sort, put a cow in the first stall, then in every stall at least d past the previous cow.
hints: Guess the minimum distance d. How would you test whether k cows fit with all gaps at least d?
Sort the stalls and place cows left to right, each in the first stall at least d after the previous cow. Placing as early as possible is never worse. Feasibility is monotone in d.
Binary search d in [1, max - min] for the largest feasible value (use mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2 when moving lo = mid). O(n log n + n log range).
pitfalls: Searching for the last true needs the upper mid, or the loop never ends when hi = lo + 1.
